info.name: mux REST API
info.description:
Postman collection for the optional local **mux** REST + WebSocket server (`mux serve`).

The server is opt-in, binds to loopback (`127.0.0.1`) by default, and — unless started with `--no-auth` — requires a local API key sent as a bearer token. It exposes mux's in-process services (endpoints, MCP servers, prompts, subagents, hooks, keybindings, skills, sessions, chat, settings) plus durable **usage telemetry** and **pricing**.

## Getting started
1. Start the server: `mux serve` (it prints the base URL and, on first run, an auto-generated API key). Or `mux serve --no-auth` for keyless local use.
2. Set the collection variables: **baseUrl** (default `http://127.0.0.1:8710`) and **apiKey** (the printed key; leave blank when using `--no-auth`).
3. Collection-level auth applies a bearer token from **apiKey** to every request except those in the **Health** folder, which is anonymous.

All paths are versioned under `/v1.0/api`. Full reference: `docs/REST_API.md`. Loopback uses `127.0.0.1` deliberately (on Windows `localhost` resolves IPv6 `::1` first and stalls).

variable.description: Scheme, host, and port the server listens on. Uses 127.0.0.1 (not localhost) to avoid Windows IPv6 first-resolution latency.
Local bearer API key printed by `mux serve`. Leave blank when the server runs with --no-auth.
An endpoint name used by the delete/chat examples.
A saved session id, used by the session export/delete examples.
A skill id, used by the skill detail/enable/delete examples.
Optional working directory for project-scoped routes (skills expand, context instructions). Blank uses the server's current directory.

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness and version. The only anonymous surface — no API key required, so this folder overrides the collection bearer auth with `noauth`.

request.description: Returns `{ Status, Product, Version, Pid, StartedUtc, Uptime, TimestampUtc }`. `Status` is `healthy` while the server is up. Use this for readiness probes; it never requires auth.

item.name: Overview
item.description: The dashboard home aggregate. One call returns the counts, default endpoint, recent sessions, derived notices, and the OpenTelemetry export status the web dashboard's home page renders. Requires the API key.

request.description: Returns the home aggregate: `Version`, `Uptime`, `AuthEnabled`, `ConfigDir`, counts (`Endpoints`, `McpServers`, `Prompts`, `Subagents`, `SkillsTotal`/`SkillsEnabled`/`SkillsInvalid`, `Hooks`, `Commands`, `Keybindings`, `Sessions`, `TotalMessages`), the default endpoint, `RecentSessions`, `Notices`, and `Observability`: `{ Enabled, ServiceName, OtlpEndpoint, Services: [ { Kind, Name, Url, Credentials } ] }`, the OpenTelemetry export status plus the bundled Grafana, Prometheus, Tempo, and Loki URLs with their local default credentials (the External services card). No secrets are returned. See TELEMETRY.md.

item.name: Endpoints
item.description: The model endpoints in `endpoints.json` — the local and cloud LLMs mux can talk to. Secrets (API keys, header values) are never returned; a blank secret on write preserves the stored value. Edits are applied as a whole-collection PUT.

request.description: Lightweight list for pickers: `{ Items: [ { Name, AdapterType, BaseUrl, Model, IsDefault } ], Count }`. No secrets.
Full editable fields for each endpoint with secrets masked (`ApiKeySet` boolean instead of the key; header values blanked). Use this as the source for the PUT round-trip.

Replaces the whole endpoint collection. Send the full list (the dashboard edits client-side, then PUTs everything). A blank `apiKey` (or blank header value) preserves the stored secret; a non-blank value overwrites it. Returns the saved, masked list.

query.description: The endpoint name to delete.

request.description: Deletes one endpoint by name. Returns the remaining masked list.

item.name: MCP Servers
item.description: MCP tool servers in `mcp-servers.json` that expose extra tools to the agent. Auth secrets are masked/preserved on the same blank-keeps-stored convention as endpoints.

request.description: Returns the configured MCP servers with any auth secret masked.
Replaces the whole MCP-server collection. Blank auth secret preserves the stored value.

Connects to a saved MCP server, runs the handshake, and lists its tools. Always 200: `Connected` reports the outcome; on failure `Error` is the one-line cause (connection refused, host not found, HTTP 401 Unauthorized, command not found on PATH) and `Details` holds the diagnosis (URL, HTTP status, Content-Type, WWW-Authenticate, Retry-After, Server, Mcp-Session-Id presence, response body, client error, stdio stderr). Secrets are never returned. 404 for an unknown name, 400 for an empty body.
Validates a definition without saving it. A blank `AuthSecret` reuses the saved server's secret with the same name.
Deletes one MCP server by name.

item.name: Prompts
item.description: System-prompt profiles in `prompts.json`. A blank system prompt inherits the built-in default.

request.description: Returns the prompt profiles (name, active flag, system prompt).
Replaces the prompt-profile collection.

item.name: Subagents
item.description: Subagent definitions in `subagents.json` the model can delegate scoped tasks to via the `spawn_subagent` tool.

request.description: Returns the subagent definitions.
Replaces the subagent collection.

item.name: Hooks & Commands
item.description: The plugin config in `hooks.json`: out-of-process event hooks and custom `/slash` commands. Saved together as one object.

request.description: Returns `{ hooks: [...], commands: [...] }`.
Replaces the plugin config.

item.name: Keybindings
item.description: Command-id → key-chord overrides in `keybindings.json`. A blank chord unbinds the command.

request.description: Returns the command-id → chord override map.
Replaces the keybinding overrides.

item.name: Skills
item.description: Skills under the skills directory — versioned Markdown-plus-code capabilities. List, inspect, toggle enablement, or delete.

request.description: Returns each skill's name, description, enabled/valid flags, and command count.
Returns one skill with its `SKILL.md` body.
Enables or disables a skill by id.
Deletes a skill folder by id.

Expands typed slash text (`/<skill> args`) into the user message that runs the skill, exactly as the terminal, desktop, and dashboard do. The skill body becomes the message with `$ARGUMENTS` and `$1`..`$9` substituted in prose (never inside code fences); a skill with commands also gets a `run_skill` hint. Project skills under `WorkingDirectory` (`.mux/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`) shadow user skills; leave `WorkingDirectory` blank to use the server's current directory. Returns `{ Matched, Skill, Arguments, Prompt, IsPlaybook }`; `Matched` is false when no usable, user-invocable skill has that name. `400` when `Input` is missing or the directory does not exist.

item.name: Context
item.description: Project context that a run in a working directory receives, such as the project instruction files (MUX.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md).

query.description: The directory to resolve instructions for. Optional; defaults to the server's current directory.

request.description: Lists the project instruction files a run in `workingDirectory` loads into its system prompt: the user-level `MUX.md` in the config directory, then `MUX.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `CLAUDE.md` (the first found) at each directory from the repository root down to the working directory. Returns `{ WorkingDirectory, Enabled, Sources, DroppedSources, TotalBytes, Truncated, Text }`. Files beyond `projectInstructionsMaxBytes` appear in `DroppedSources`, outermost first. `400` when the directory does not exist.

query.description: The text typed after @. Optional; empty lists top-level entries.
The directory paths are relative to. Optional; defaults to the server's current directory.
The most paths to return, 1 to 100. Optional; defaults to 20.

request.description: Completion for @ file mentions: project paths matching `prefix`, best first, with forward slashes; directories end with `/`. Dependency and build folders are never offered. Returns `{ WorkingDirectory, Prefix, Paths, Mentions }`. `400` when the directory does not exist or `max` is out of range. Chat routes resolve @path mentions server-side.

query.description: Selects the project scope. Optional; defaults to the server's current directory.
Optional: words that must all appear (case-insensitive).

request.description: Returns `{ WorkingDirectory, ProjectKey, Enabled, Memories }`: the project's memories, then the global ones, newest first within each. `query` keeps only memories containing every word; `name` returns one memory (404 when there is none). `400` when the directory does not exist.

body.raw:
{
  "Name": "test-command",
  "Description": "Run tests with dotnet test src/Mux.sln",
  "Content": "Run tests with dotnet test src/Mux.sln; they take about four minutes.",
  "Scope": "project",
  "WorkingDirectory": "{{workingDirectory}}"
}

request.description: Creates a memory (201) or updates the one whose name slugs the same (200). `Scope` is `project` (default) or `global`. Returns the saved `MemoryDto`.

query.description: The memory's name.
Optional: project or global. Without it, the project scope is tried first.
Selects the project scope.

request.description: Deletes a memory and returns it. `404` when no memory has that name.

item.name: Sessions
item.description: Persisted chat sessions under `~/.mux/sessions`. List, export to HTML/Markdown, or delete.

request.description: Returns saved sessions (id, title, endpoint, model, timestamps).

Incrementally edits a session's labels and tags: adds/removes labels and sets (upsert by key)/removes tags. Tag keys are normalized (lowercased, slugified); labels dedupe case-insensitively. Returns the updated session summary. 404 for an unknown id, 400 when a label/tag fails normalization.

query.description: md or html

request.description: Renders a session to `{ format, filename, content }` for download.
Deletes a session by id.

item.name: Chat
item.description: A plain, tool-free chat completion against a configured endpoint — for the dashboard chat surface. It does not run the agent loop or expose tools.

request.description: Streams the completion server-side and returns the buffered result plus timing: `{ role, content, endpoint, model, stats: { ttftMs, streamingMs, totalMs, inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens } }`. This call is also recorded to usage telemetry (call kind `chat`).

item.name: Settings
item.description: The editable settings subset over `settings.json`. Secrets are masked (for example `rest.apiKeySet` instead of the key); the REST API key changes only when a non-blank `rest.apiKey` is supplied.

request.description: Returns the current settings with secrets masked.
Updates settings (validated/clamped, written to settings.json). Send only the fields you intend to change.

item.name: Usage Telemetry
item.description:
Read-only analytics over the shared usage database (`~/.mux/usage.db`), written by every mux instance on the machine. Every query accepts a time window as explicit `from`/`to` (Unix epoch **milliseconds**) or a `range` keyword (`hour`|`day`|`week`|`month`|`all`), plus optional `endpoint`, `model`, and `callKind` filters. When telemetry is disabled these endpoints return empty results (and `/filters` reports `Enabled: false`).

Every `Metrics` object carries: `Calls`, `Errors`, `ErrorRate`, `InputTokens`, `CachedTokens`, `OutputTokens`, `TotalTokens`, `CostUsd`, `CacheHitRate`, `AvgTtftMs`, `P50/P95/P99TtftMs`, `AvgTotalMs`, `P50/P95/P99TotalMs`, `AvgStreamMs`, `AvgTokensPerSec`.

query.description: primary|compaction|subagent|chat|probe
Scope to one session id.
Comma-separated labels; matches sessions carrying them (AND).
Comma-separated key:value tags; matches sessions carrying them (AND).

request.description: Window KPI summary: `{ FromUnixMs, ToUnixMs, Metrics }`. Backs the dashboard KPI strip and the TUI /usage view.

query.description: hour or day
Scope to one session id.
Comma-separated labels; matches sessions carrying them (AND).
Comma-separated key:value tags; matches sessions carrying them (AND).

request.description: Bucketed series for charting: `{ Items: [ { BucketStartUnixMs, Metrics } ], Count }`.

query.description: model|endpoint|provider|command|callkind|label|tag

request.description: Totals grouped by a dimension, sorted by cost: `{ Items: [ { Dimension, Value, Metrics } ], Count }`.

query.description: true|false
Scope to one session id.
Comma-separated labels; matches sessions carrying them (AND).
Comma-separated key:value tags; matches sessions carrying them (AND).

request.description: Paginated raw per-call history (newest first) with derived `CostUsd` per row: `{ Items, TotalCount, PageNumber, PageSize }`.

query.description: The usage-event row id to delete (from an events row's Id).

request.description: Deletes one recorded call by its row id. Returns `{ Deleted: <count> }`.
Distinct endpoints and models seen in the store, for filter controls, plus `{ Enabled }` (false when telemetry is disabled).

item.name: Pricing
item.description: The user-editable model pricing table in `pricing.json` used to derive usage cost at read time. **Note:** unlike most mux DTOs, pricing serializes camelCase (`version`, `models`, `inputPerMTok`, `cachedInputPerMTok`, `outputPerMTok`).

request.description: Returns `{ version, models: { "<model>": { inputPerMTok, cachedInputPerMTok, outputPerMTok } } }` (curated defaults when the file is absent).
Replaces the whole pricing table. Rates are USD per million tokens. Returns the saved table. A rate change re-values historical cost immediately (cost is computed at read time).

item.name: Runs
item.description: List, inspect, and cancel active and recently-finished runs. Set the {{runId}} variable from a chat stream's `run` event. The live WebSocket event bridge at `/v1.0/ws` is not exercisable from Postman — see docs/REST_API.md for its subscribe/approve protocol.

request.description: Active and recently-finished runs as summaries, most-recently-started first. Returns `{ Items: [ { RunId, SessionId, EndpointName, Model, Status, IsTerminal, StartedUtc, CompletedUtc } ], Count }`. Terminal runs are retained ~5 minutes then evicted.
Full live state of one run: status, counters, current tool, last error, and the task-plan checklist. `404` when the run is unknown or has been evicted.

Cooperatively cancel a run: trips its cancellation token and publishes a terminal `run_completed` (status `canceled`) to stream subscribers. `200` `{ Ok, RunId, Status }` on success; `404` when the run is unknown or already finished.
